sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Cheatham County?
sections.html:
File deeds and mortgages for Cheatham County property with the Register of Deeds in Ashland City, 354 Frey Street, Suite C. Weekday hours run 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and the phone number is (615) 792-4317.

A seller usually needs two more offices, and both share the building. The Trustee is in Suite A, (615) 792-4298. The Assessor of Property is in Suite B, (615) 792-5371. Ashland City is the county seat, and the other incorporated places are Kingston Springs, Pegram and Pleasant View.

sections.h2: What the Register of Deeds does and does not do
sections.html:
This office files legal instruments, chiefly the ones that transfer title to land, and maintains the public index. Many of its duties are listed in Tennessee Code section 8-13-108, with further ones in other statutes.

  • Staff cannot write, alter or revise a deed. They are barred from practicing law, so drafting is left to an attorney or title company.
  • No title searches either. Employees will help you spot recorded instruments that could be liens, but the actual search is work for a title company or attorney.
  • The index runs by name alone. If all you have is an address, the county Assessor at (615) 792-5371 can find the parcel.
  • Only a signed, authenticated original goes on record. The single exception is a certified copy of a document that another government office has already filed.

What it costs to record depends on the kind of document. Phone (615) 792-4317 for a quote before mailing a deed. Copy charges are low.

Service or taxAmount
Plain copy$0.15 per page
Large plat copy$5.00 per page
Certified copy$1.00 per page
Realty transfer tax37 cents for each $100 transferred
Mortgage tax11.5 cents for each $100 of debt beyond $2,000

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies when a house sells?
sections.html:
When Tennessee real estate changes hands, the state collects 37 cents on every $100, measured against whichever is larger, the sale price or the appraised worth. Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409 places this inside the recordation tax. Debt that gets recorded, a deed of trust for instance, is taxed too, at 11.5 cents per $100 after the first $2,000 is excluded.

The contract settles who covers each tax. The closing agent can quote the exact numbers, so ask early. Transfer tax tends to be the largest recording-related charge. The county's median home value is $338,700, which gives a feel for the price range.

sections.h2: How county property tax fits into a sale
sections.html:
Property tax billing belongs to the Trustee and valuation belongs to the Assessor, so skip the Register's counter for either. The Trustee bills whoever holds title on January 1. A purchase contract may hand the cost to the other side, yet the Trustee never sees those side agreements. Anyone who buys or sells during the year is told to confirm that the tax is paid whether or not a bill arrived.

Pay the 2026 bill at the Trustee's office by Friday, February 26, 2027 to avoid interest, or at a bank through February 28, 2027. After that, 1.5 percent is added each month. A parcel remains with the Trustee for a full year of delinquency before it goes to the delinquent tax attorney, who files a Chancery Court suit between March 16 and March 31. For a specific parcel's balance, call (615) 792-4298.

Trustee hours differ by day: 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Monday and Wednesday, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Tuesday and Thursday, and 8 a.m. to noon on Friday. Because owner names get recorded with varied spellings, the Trustee suggests keeping your own list of every parcel you bought or sold during the year. Sellers should bring the bill to closing.

sections.h2: How recorded deeds feed the assessment
sections.html:
Down the hall, the Assessor relies on what the Register files. The office's brochure names comparing similar sales as its main valuation method, using the hundreds of sales recorded each year. Your recorded deed becomes one more comparison point in the next reappraisal.

Reappraisal happens every five years, and 2019 is the year the brochure gives for the most recent one before printing. Phone the Assessor at (615) 792-5371 to learn the current cycle. Start a value dispute with the Assessor. If that fails, the county Board of Equalization takes cases from June onward. It weighs value alone and cannot touch the rate.

Those who qualify for state Tax Relief file at the Trustee's office. That group covers low-income elderly and disabled homeowners and disabled veteran owners or their surviving spouses, and the house must be the primary residence.

About 42,778 people lived in the county as of July 2025, with 18,310 housing units. Between 2020 and 2024 the county counted 16,279 households, $89,852 in median household income and $1,345 in median gross rent. A high 81.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and 285 building permits were issued in 2025.

sections.h2: What to prepare before the deed is recorded
sections.html:
Hand over the signed original deed with a clear legal description and the price paid, so the tax can be worked out. Double-check how each party's name is spelled, since anyone searching the index will type a name.

  • Find out from the Register what fee applies to the deed and to a release of an earlier mortgage.
  • Get a payoff from your lender and a tax status letter from the Trustee.
  • Pay off any overdue county tax before the deed is recorded.
  • If a lender or court wants a certified copy, it costs $1.00 per page.

Few sellers ever stand at the Register's counter. After signing, the closing agent or title company carries the deed over, staff index it, and the new owner shows up in the record under the name written on the instrument.

sections.h2: Step by step: recording after a sale
sections.html:
Here is how a typical Cheatham County sale moves from signing to the public record.

  1. An attorney or title company writes the deed, because the Register's staff cannot.
  2. Buyer and seller sign, and the signature is authenticated so the instrument is eligible for recording.
  3. At closing, the agent calculates transfer tax on the price or value and collects it alongside the recording fee.
  4. Any lender payoff and overdue county tax are cleared from the proceeds.
  5. The signed original goes to 354 Frey Street, Suite C, where staff record it and add it to the name index.

For anything out of the ordinary, like a release of an old mortgage or a document with several parties, call ahead and get the fee quoted.

faqs.q: Where is the Cheatham County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is at 354 Frey Street, Suite C, Ashland City, TN 37015. It is staffed weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and answers at (615) 792-4317.

faqs.q: How much is the Tennessee transfer tax in Cheatham County?
faqs.a: It is 37 cents per $100, applied to the price or the property's value, whichever is larger. The closing agent will compute the dollar amount for your own deal.

faqs.q: Can the Cheatham County Register of Deeds write my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office cannot prepare, change or revise a deed because Tennessee prohibits the staff from practicing law. Use an attorney or title company.

faqs.q: Can I search Cheatham County deed records by address?
faqs.a: Not there, because the Register's indexes are by name. The Cheatham County Assessor of Property at (615) 792-5371 can look up a parcel by address.

faqs.q: How much does a certified copy cost in Cheatham County?
faqs.a: A certified copy is $1.00 a page. Plain copies are 15 cents a page and large plat copies are $5.00.
